clue.text: Good memory required by opera house producing the Ring?

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in a computer
the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera House

explanation.surface: A singer needs a good memory for an opera house staging Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' looks like Wagner's operas, which suit the opera house; the question mark signals that it is just an ordinary ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a metal or plastic eyelet, a small reinforcing ring set into a hole.

clue.text: Sensitive area gynaecologist's first to see

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A doctor wants to examine a tender place before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gynaecologist's first' gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an erogenous zone said to be especially sensitive.

clue.text: Expulsion got us in trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are disturbed and jumbled

explanation.surface: Being thrown out landed us in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges GOT US IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting is the act of driving someone out of a position, an expulsion.

clue.text: Fur from an emporium in Knightsbridge

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fur coat bought at a smart London department store.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHTSBRIDGE is a wealthy London district, home of Harrods.
explanation.definitionFit: Mink is the prized fur of a small semi-aquatic mammal.

clue.text: Novel format for TS Eliot, though he is novel

indicators.note: format means the letters are set out in a new form

explanation.surface: A novel adapted for the poet, though he writes poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'format' rearranges TS ELIOT and THOUGH HE together; 'is novel' adds that the result is a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's 1927 work is a famous English novel.

clue.text: Bird almost right by vessel

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a title is a right or legal claim to something
Noah's ark is the classic vessel

explanation.surface: A bird watcher notes something nearly on the right next to a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of TITLE, leaving TITL.
explanation.definitionFit: The titlark is an old name for the meadow pipit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Prolix speech before 1912?

parts.note: read as a sum: nineteen placed before twelve, a dozen, describing rapid wordy chatter

explanation.surface: Long-winded talk from before the Titanic sank.
explanation.walkthrough: The date 1912 is read as 19 to 12, nineteen before the dozen, the idiom for chattering endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone speaking very fast and without stopping.

clue.text: See 5
He has an objective — to go round a city in California

indicators.note: to go round means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: an aim is an objective
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man whose purpose is to tour a Californian city.
explanation.walkthrough: AN AIM goes round HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaheim is a city in southern California, home of Disneyland.

clue.text: Grand railway starts to provide trains working with gas

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, and a grand is a thousand

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the following words

parts.note: on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A big railway begins running trains on gas power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' is a thousand pounds, K; 'starts to' takes P and T from 'provide trains'.
explanation.definitionFit: Krypton is a noble gas, an element found in tiny amounts in air.

clue.text: Letters somewhere in Brazil after delivery

parts.note: letters that come by mail are the post
Natal is a city in north-eastern Brazil

explanation.surface: Mail somewhere in Brazil arrives once it has been delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' reads as the postman's round, which suits 'Letters'; it means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Postnatal describes the period following childbirth, which is a delivery in the obstetric sense.

clue.text: Creep to a back yard

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is written in reverse order

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off to a garden at the rear of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of 'back yard' but turns YD into DY. 'Creep' looks like a verb; here it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A creep is a sycophant, someone who fawns on superiors, exactly what a toady does.

clue.text: Cotton on a stick

definitions.meaning: to cotton on is to grasp or realise, informally
a small thin branch or stick

explanation.definitionFit: To twig is British slang for to understand, and a twig is also a slender piece of wood.

clue.text: Entire term wasted in seclusion

indicators.note: wasted suggests the letters are ruined and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A whole term spent idly in isolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' rearranges the letters of ENTIRE and TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement can mean withdrawal from society, a state of privacy and seclusion.

clue.text: Slapstick item in sad picture isn't right

indicators.note: isn't right means the letters are wrong, out of order

explanation.surface: A gloomy film that lacks something about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't right' rearranges SAD and PICTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie in the face is the classic prop of slapstick comedy.

clue.text: A complaint by one relative of guinea pig

parts.note: gout is a painful medical complaint of the joints
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a family member who is a guinea pig in experiments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an illness, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a South American rodent closely related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Saint Benny?

definitions.meaning: a saint is a virtuous person
Benny is the bandleader clarinettist known as the King of Swing

explanation.definitionFit: Benny Goodman was the famous swing clarinettist, and a saintly person is a thoroughly good man.

clue.text: To enthral a malicious woman we held back

indicators.note: held means one piece is gripped inside another

parts.note: a bitch is slang for a spiteful woman

indicators.note: back means the little word is written in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman whom we restrained tries to captivate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the little word and 'held' sets it inside the woman. 'To' is the infinitive marker that lets 'enthral' stand as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch is to cast a spell over, to captivate or enthral someone.

clue.text: Is clumsy butcher first with entrails?

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: umbles are the edible offal of a deer

explanation.surface: A butcher fumbles while handling offal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher first' gives B; UMBLES are old word for animal innards (as in humble pie).
explanation.definitionFit: To bumble is to move or act in an awkward, blundering way.

clue.text: Churchill gains a lot of weight

parts.note: to gain is to win
a ton is a large weight

explanation.surface: The wartime leader is getting heavier.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill's first name is the answer; the surface paints a man putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Winston Churchill was the wartime British prime minister.

clue.text: One's cold to walk over

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: over signals that the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to pace is to walk steadily

explanation.surface: Someone says a surface is chilly to walk across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PACE into ECAP. The whole clue is the definition too: a polar sheet of ice is a cold thing to cross on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar sheet of permanent ice is a famously cold expanse that explorers trek across.

clue.text: Someone else on a roundabout before the ride starts

indicators.note: roundabout means the two words are turned back to front
starts means only the initial letter is used

explanation.surface: A person on a fairground carousel before the ride begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a roundabout' turns ON A into ANO.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means one more or a different person, someone else.

clue.text: Chap engaged in battle with Denmark, Sweden, Norway etc

indicators.note: engaged in means one piece is held within another

parts.note: Mons was a First World War battle in Belgium
Archie is a man's name, standing in for any chap

explanation.surface: A man fights in a war involving the Scandinavian countries.
explanation.walkthrough: MONS is a First World War battle in Belgium; 'Chap' needs a specific man's name to go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark, Sweden and Norway are all kingdoms, each ruled by a hereditary sovereign.

clue.text: Pugilist knocking out unknown South African

indicators.note: knocking out means a letter is removed

parts.note: a pugilist is a boxer
X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: A fighter flattens an anonymous South African opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking out' suits a boxer but here removes X from BOXER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boer is a South African of Dutch descent, an Afrikaner farmer.

clue.text: Majestic poem or the reverse

indicators.note: the reverse means the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: a lay is a narrative poem or song

explanation.surface: A stately poem, or perhaps its opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: LAY OR read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal means befitting a monarch, regal or majestic.

clue.text: Sportsmen who are paid for writing? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls one letter short at the end

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language

explanation.surface: Professional athletes who earn money as authors, or almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of PROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Professional sportspeople are paid for playing, unlike amateurs.

clue.text: New tulip bulb may be

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh tulip bulb might grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulb' looks like the tulip's bulb; it is a light bulb, which may be switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric light bulb, when switched on, is illuminated.

clue.text: Dig up only half? That's weird

parts.note: to dig up is to unearth

indicators.note: half means only part of the word, here its second half, is used

explanation.surface: Excavating just part of a site turns up something strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the back half of 'only'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthly means supernatural or eerie, and so strange or weird.

clue.text: True as scripture

parts.note: as and since both mean because
RE is religious education, the school subject

explanation.surface: A claim that something is as true as holy writ.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject of religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine or heartfelt, true in the sense of honest and loyal.

clue.text: Breathtaking passage under a bridge

parts.note: read literally: a passage that takes in breath, lying beneath the bridge of the nose

explanation.surface: A stunning stretch of river beneath a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathtaking' suggests stunning scenery, but it means taking in air; the bridge is the nose's.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose is an air passage sitting just below the bony bridge.
